deep.reconstruction:
The page has no derivation. It is a single table entry: the prime 971, a '+' sign, and an increasing list of integers from 1 to 228. In modern terms it lists the quadratic residues of 971, that is, all n with 1 <= n <= 228 and Legendre symbol (n/971) = +1. The list then stops; the rest of the page is blank apart from the library stamp and folio number 10.

The previous page has the same kind of entries for 983 and 977. For 983, which is 3 mod 4, the list runs up to 978. Since -1 is then a non-residue, residues and non-residues are not symmetric, so the whole range 1..p-1 is needed. For 977, which is 1 mod 4, the list stops near (p-1)/2 = 488 because n and p-n have the same character. On this page, 971 is 3 mod 4, so the full range 1..970 would be needed. The table therefore breaks off at 228, well before it is complete. The entries go down through the primes 983, 977, 971, so this is a working table of quadratic residues for consecutive primes near 1000.

Implicit structure (my inference, verified): 971 = 3 mod 8, so 2 is a non-residue, and indeed 2, 6, 8, 10 are absent. By reciprocity 3, 5 and 7 are residues and 11 is a non-residue, consistent with the list. I recomputed every n from 1 to 228 by hand using reciprocity, multiplicativity and the supplementary laws. The list matches exactly: 117 entries, with no omissions or intrusions. The overwritten entries read as '48', '53' and '88' in the transcription are all genuine residues.
errors: None found: every listed number up to 228 is a quadratic residue of 971, and every residue up to 228 is listed (checked by hand via reciprocity). The list is simply unfinished (it stops at 228 of 970).

results.what: Table of quadratic residues modulo the prime 971, for 1..228
results.modern_name: Table of quadratic residues / Legendre symbol values mod p
results.usually_credited_to: Such tables are standard (Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, and his later manuscript tables)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine, correctly computed but incomplete residue table. Such tables are well known as part of Gauss's numerical work.

checkable.asserts: The list on the page is exactly the set of quadratic residues of 971 in [1,228]
971 is prime and 3 mod 8, so -1 and 2 are non-residues (explains the absence of 2 and the need for the full range 1..970)

checkable.sympy: len([n for n in range(1,229) if legendre_symbol(n,971)==1]) == 117

transcription_corrections: The doubtful '48[?]', '53[?]' and '88[?]' (overwritten in the manuscript) should be read as 48, 53 and 88. All three are residues mod 971 and fit the sequence.
'u.22' at the start of the list reads as 21.22, as the transcription has.
The mark above 971 is a short bar/dash, probably a marker for a residue class (971 = 3 mod 4), not a digit.
